newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thousands of Germans return home as floods recede.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Germans return home as floods recede.

text.p: Thousands of Germans forced to flee flooding three weeks ago were allowed to go home on Saturday as water levels on the Oder River receded.
Dikes preventing the swollen river gushing into the Oderbruch basin east of Berlin were no longer in danger of bursting, the Brandenburg state interior ministry in Potsdam said.

Authorities gave about 5,000 people the all-clear to return to their homes in the agricultural area on Germany's frontier with Poland, and said many had already returned without waiting for permission.
Six villages were partially or totally submerged and 7,200 hectares (18,000 acres) inundated by the worst flooding in memory in the region. Large tracts of farmland were ruined.

The total damage has yet to be calculated, but officials fear it could run into billions of marks (dollars). Germany did, however, escape the more serious havoc which the floods wreaked in the neighbouring Czech Republic and Poland, where more than 100 people died.

Of the 160 km (100 miles) of dikes which held back most of the water on the German side, 3.5 km were destroyed and will have to be rebuilt and another five km will need repairs, at a cost of at least 132 million marks ($72 million), state officials said.
On the other side of the Oder in the Polish town of Slubice, many of the 16,000 evacuees who fled the rising waters two weeks ago were also returning to their homes.

Water levels dropped along the Oder for the sixth consecutive day on Saturday. South of Frankfurt an der Oder in the Ziltendorf basin, where the worst of the German flooding occurred, it was falling by one cm (0.4 inches) an hour.
German soldiers continued to monitor the dikes, which they have spent the last three weeks trying to reinforce with sandbags, logs and gravel.
Brandenburg's interior minister Alwin Ziel said 55,000 people had donated 7.8 million marks ($4.2 million) so far to help the German flood victims. ($ = 1.844 German Marks)
